lines: Statim makes 68 decisions per second on one RTX 3070.
Developers hate installing Python stacks and huge weights that delay their apps until you load.
Statim is a native C++20 engine for System-1 decision models that lets you switch existing clients by changing the base URL.
The state and questions become one token sequence with a mask per option.
Watch it answer typed questions about text or JSON to pick a label like billing with 0.9948 probability.
On S1Bench the multilingual model scores 0.638 macro accuracy above its untuned Laya base.
Statim cold starts in 0.76 seconds while Laya waits 11.35 seconds to answer.
It loads a 5.5 MB binary plus one GGUF file to keep memory low.
It runs on Linux x86-64 with AVX2. A TypeScript client SDK retries 503 responses with backoff.
Apache-2.0 licence is free for any use, built by BEKO2210 with one GitHub star.
Download the 3 MB binary and run statim serve with your model file.
Save this for a team tired of loading Python stacks.
Statim answers in a tiny C++ binary with zero Python.
